title: snapgit
subtitle: GitHub, but disappearing is a feature.
narration: Introducing snapgit. Git meets Snapchat. Because if your code is going to vanish, it should at least be on purpose.

title: Lately, GitHub has been disappearing on its own
items: Aug 6: Actions and Pages, queued jobs, impact around 10 hours
Aug 17: roughly 20% errors on web and API, 50% on archive downloads
Oct 7: webhooks, Actions and pull requests degraded
narration: Lately, GitHub has been disappearing on its own. On August sixth, queued Actions jobs and throttled webhooks, with impact lasting around ten hours. On August seventeenth, roughly twenty percent errors on the website and A P I, and fifty percent on archive downloads. And on October seventh, webhooks, Actions and pull requests were degraded again.

title: The scoreboard
narration: One tracker counted two hundred fifty seven incidents in twelve months, forty eight of them major. February twenty twenty six alone had thirty seven.

quote: Your code was going to disappear anyway.
sub: Now you get to pick when.
narration: Here is the thing. Your work was always going to disappear at some point. snapgit just lets you pick when.

title: Disappearing branches
code:
$ snapgit snap wip/hot-take --ttl 2h
📸 wip/hot-take will disappear in 2h (2026-10-10 20:03Z). Commit fast.

$ snapgit ls
wip/hot-take                   c3edc4e  2h left
narration: Start a branch with a self destruct timer. Two hours, then it's gone. A real git branch, with a real countdown.

title: Gone. Locally and on the remote.
code:
$ snapgit extend wip/hot-take 1h
⏳ wip/hot-take now disappears 2026-10-10 21:03Z

(four hours later)
$ snapgit sweep --remote origin
👻 ghosted wip/hot-take (was c3edc4e, remote too). Undo: git branch wip/hot-take c3edc4e
narration: Need more time? Extend it. Otherwise, the sweep ghosts the branch, on your machine and on the remote, and hands you the commit hash in case you regret it. Hooks make it automatic.

title: Pull requests with one button
code:
$ snapgit pr send fix/login -m "Fix login" -r origin
📨 sent "Fix login" (fix/login -> main)
   id 95962cb1, readable once. Unless rejected, it merges into main at 2026-10-11 18:15Z
   recipient: snapgit pr open 95962cb1 -r origin   (or snapgit pr reject 95962cb1 -r origin)
$ snapgit pr open 95962cb1
Fix login   #95962cb1, read once
  78a8ca1 fix login
+export const login = () => "ok";
💥 the contents just self-destructed. You will not see them again.
⏳ the PR is still live: it merges into main at 2026-10-11 18:15Z unless you run: snapgit pr reject 95962cb1
narration: Pull requests, with exactly one button. Send one, and the branch goes on the clock. The recipient can read it once, and then the contents burn. The pull request itself stays alive.

title: The button is reject
code:
$ snapgit pr reject b85ca565 -m 'no'
🚫 rejected. It will not be merged (the sender hears about it when their branch expires)

$ snapgit pr receipts
👀 Alice <alice@example.com> opened "Fix login" (#95962cb1) at 2026-10-10 18:15Z
receipts shown once, now deleted
narration: The button is reject. No approve. No L G T M. No changes requested. And you still get a read receipt, so you know who looked.

title: Merge by neglect
code:
(a day later)
$ snapgit sweep --remote origin
🔀 PR 95962cb1: nobody rejected it, so fix/login merged into main and was pushed
👻 ghosted fix/login (was 78a8ca1, remote too). Undo: git branch fix/login 78a8ca1
🚫 PR b85ca565 rejected by Bob <bob@example.com>: "no". Nothing merged
👻 ghosted rewrite-in-rust (was 732f08a, remote too). Undo: git branch rewrite-in-rust 732f08a
$ git log --oneline --graph -4
*   ecde4d3 Merge fix/login into main
|\  
| * 78a8ca1 fix login
|/  
* b4f7492 init
narration: And if nobody rejects it? When the branch self destructs, it merges. Merge by neglect. A rejected one dies with its branch, and nothing lands.

title: Streaks. Stories.
code:
$ snapgit streak
🔥 1 day streak. Longest: 1.

$ snapgit story
📖 your story, last 1d
   ecde4d3  Merge fix/login into main  (origin/main)
   b4f7492  init  (no branch tip)
   78a8ca1  fix login  (no branch tip)
   🔥 1 day streak
   (this story will not be saved)
narration: Then your streak, and your story: your last day in git, which will not be saved.

title: Under the hood, it's just git
items: Opening a PR claims a receipt ref with a create-only push, so only one reader wins
The deadline is the branch timer; expiry merges with plain git
Timers live in your git config; hooks sweep for you
No servers, so there is nothing to take down
narration: Under the hood, it's just git. The first reader claims the pull request with an atomic push, so only one person ever sees the contents. The deadline is the branch timer, and expiry merges with plain git. Timers live in your git config. Zero dependencies, and no servers, so there is nothing for us to take down.

title: Downtime, compared
colB_body:
Disappears on purpose
Scheduled, by you
For as long as you said
narration: The difference? GitHub disappears unexpectedly. snapgit disappears on purpose, on a schedule you chose.

subtitle: Try snapgit
narration: Try snapgit. Clone it, link it, and start a branch with a timer. It's hosted on GitHub. We know.
